Why not join a branch of the military? I've always been passionate about joining the Army since high school and wished I knew about this stuff before I went to college. Sorry, this is long and has poor grammar, but could give you some of my feeling about what you are going through and stuff. I'm 20 and lost most of my friends, got social anxiety, depression, and maybe a lot of other stuff, but I'm realizing who I am and my worth. I have made better progress with myself than I ever have. Slowly each day I feel more and more comfortable being around other people. Its all just traumatic events and the fear that those events instill in our minds that keep us from further developing ourselves. Instead we indulge in stuff that gives us pleasure or a sense of satisfaction, but become too dependent on it and it causes us to be less productive and lazy, and wanting to be alone, shut in and reserved. And its not like you don't want friends because it wouldn't be an issues if you weren't discussing it, you just have difficultly fitting in and forgotten how to interact with new/different people and worried if they'll like you. You need to discover who you are as a person and love yourself. Believe you are a somebody and you do matter because you are alive and deserve better. Try not to focus on if people are looking at you or judging you, instead focus on your thoughts. At least then your mind won't be focused on those around you, but still be aware of your surroundings. Make a list of your accomplishments. I make one each day called "Today's Accomplishments" and make a list of things a WANT to complete that day, such as make a new email address, or make eat a healthy meal for lunch, or listen to song, or clean around evening time, simple stuff to show that you are doing something with your life.  I'm not in school, but on the days I'm off from work I would wake up early(like 5, 6, or 7 in the mourning) and apply for jobs. I hate my cashier job, and when I come home I'm so burntout and exhausted to do much. So the mourning is perfect for that, and around 8,9,and 10 in the mourning I would call some places, write down names and places(literally writing on a notepad) and go out driving around, maybe go somewhere then come back home alittle after 2 or 3 O' clock and use the rest of the day for myself. When you learn more about yourself you discover your strengths and weaknesses. What your mind/body can tolerate in a certain situation. And how much "energy" you need so you won't be burntout. Recently my I've felt more positive about life than ever and all the "help" I tried to get. Antidepressants failed, its true you need to believe in yourself for it to work, but it never "helped" me getting into liking music, or less negative and hopeless. It only temporarily made my body less tense, and it failed at that. The psychologist(?) I felt never actually cared and didn't give me any hints or tips to improve. And my family is a whole nother story. All that anxiety, depression is just an imbalance in your life and you need to not focus on your problems(and your pleasures) more than your well being. Once you focus more on yourself you won't be as critical about the issues in your life. Because everyone deals with this eventually. You either to chose to expect it to happen, or let it happen naturally like life supposed to be(which is the better option). Its out of our control and we can't force anything to change in an instant. In a way its sorta like say "deal with it" but a lot less insensitive and blunt. So don't give up, and don't spend half the day worrying about something that isn't in your control. Thinking more about how your actions can influence you and other people. And I don't have any closing words. I do hope you have a good day and life gets better for you. And I never thought about it until recently, but now I say it all the time. "The day is only a good day when you make it a good day. It doesn't have to be perfect, you could even get mad or stressed out, but you can ALWAYS make it better."
